meta.title: Tide-aware cancellations
meta.lede: The change cancels a Brisk sailing on its own when low water leaves too little depth at the ramp for the Gannet. Six findings, one of them a blocker. Approve or rework, then rule on each by number.

parts.markdown:
Joss's change adds a job that reads the tide table every hour and cancels any Brisk sailing where the depth at the ramp falls below the Gannet's draft plus a safety margin. Reviewed at revision `4e1c9a2`, with the tests run locally.

The tide table importer was reviewed on its own last month and is not covered here.

parts.title: What changed
rows: Finds when each sailing is at the ramp and the depth at that time.
Cancels a sailing that fails the check and records why.
Covers a spring tide, a neap tide, and a missing table.
Adds the Gannet's draft and the safety margin.

items.title: Tide times compared in UTC against local sailing times
items.summary: Sailing times are local and tide times are UTC, so in summer time every check looks at the wrong hour.

facets.label: Where
facets.markdown: `booking/tide/window.go`, line 58, in `depthAt`.

facets.label: Why it matters
facets.markdown: From March to October the job reads the depth an hour away from departure. A sailing at low water can pass the check, and the Gannet can ground at the ramp.

facets.label: Fix
facets.markdown: Convert the departure to the harbour's time zone before the lookup, and keep tide times with their zone.

facets.label: Evidence
facets.markdown: The spring tide test passes only because its fixture is in January. Moved to 14 July, the 06:05 sailing reads 2.9 m where the table gives 1.7 m.

facets.label: Diff
facets.markdown:
```diff
-	at := sailing.Departs
+	at := sailing.Departs.In(harbour.Zone)
 	depth := table.DepthAt(at.UTC())
```

items.title: Riders get no notice when the job cancels a sailing
items.summary: The job sets the sailing's status directly and skips the notice path, so riders learn at the harbour.

facets.label: Where
facets.markdown: `booking/cancel/auto.go`, in `Cancel`, which writes the status instead of calling `cancel.Sailing`.

facets.label: Why it matters
facets.markdown: A cancellation at 05:00 for the 07:40 reaches nobody. Riders drive to Varre and find the ramp closed.

facets.label: Fix
facets.markdown: Call `cancel.Sailing` with the reason `tide`, which sends the plain notice with its free rebooking link.

items.title: The Gannet's draft is read once at startup
items.summary: Changing the draft or the margin needs a deploy, and the harbour master changes the margin with the season.

facets.label: Where
facets.markdown: `config/vessels.yaml`, loaded in `booking/cmd/serve/main.go`, line 41.

facets.label: Why it matters
facets.markdown: The harbour master raises the margin in winter swell. Today that takes a release, on the very day it matters most.

facets.label: Fix
facets.markdown: Read vessel limits from the settings table the office already edits, and log each change with who made it.

items.title: No backoff when the tide table is missing
items.summary: When next month's table has not arrived, the job retries every second and floods the logs.

facets.label: Where
facets.markdown: `booking/cancel/auto.go`, line 112, the retry loop in `Run`.

facets.label: Why it matters
facets.markdown: The table arrives by email once a month and was late twice last year. The job would log 86,400 errors a day and quietly check nothing.

facets.label: Fix
facets.markdown: Back off to hourly, alert the office once, and show a banner that tide checks are off.

items.title: The 0.4 metre margin has no source
items.summary: The safety margin is a bare number, and nothing says where it came from or when it should change.

facets.label: Where
facets.markdown: `config/vessels.yaml`, line 9.

facets.label: Why it matters
facets.markdown: The next person to touch it will guess. The harbour master's letter from May sets 0.4 m in summer and 0.6 m from November.

facets.label: Fix
facets.markdown: Name it `ramp_margin_m`, set both seasons, and link the letter in a comment.

items.title: Test names describe the code, not the tide
items.summary: Names like TestRun2 hide which tide each test covers.

facets.label: Where
facets.markdown: `booking/cancel/auto_test.go`, all four tests.

facets.label: Why it matters
facets.markdown: When a test fails next year, its name should say which tide broke. Renaming costs a minute now.

facets.label: Fix
facets.markdown: Rename them after the tide they cover, such as `TestSpringLowWaterCancels` and `TestNeapTideSails`.

items.title: Who can undo a tide cancellation
items.summary: Only the harbour office role can reinstate a sailing, and a test covers it.

items.title: Database migration
items.summary: The new reason column is nullable and backfills nothing, so it deploys without downtime.

items.title: Metrics and logs
items.summary: Each run logs the sailings checked and cancelled, and a counter feeds the existing dashboard.

items.title: Holm and Keddle sailings
items.summary: Left alone, as intended: both ramps have enough depth at every tide.
